issues.display_title: Issue #1785: Rebuild failed-payment auto-cancel cron for Stripe in GoThru-API-New
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Cron that auto-cancels Stripe subscriptions on failed payment and closes out any pending unsubscribe row, replacing the retired gothru.co cancel cron. Remaining work is putting it on a schedule and confirming email delivery once the template exists.

Current state

On main, there's no equivalent to the legacy failed-payment auto-cancel logic — nothing in GoThru-API-New checks Stripe for failed payments or processes queued unsubscribe rows. The old gothru.co cron that used to handle this is fully shut down, so failed payments and pending downgrades currently just pile up unhandled.

Target state

  • New cron endpoint (GET /cronjob/process-unsubscribes-table) runs in two phases: find Stripe subscriptions with a genuinely failed payment and queue them, then process every pending unsubscribe row (from any source, not just this cron) and apply the account downgrade.
  • Supports safe dry-run and test-mode checks before writing anything for real.
  • Checked against real production data on 2026-08-19 — both the detected candidates and the row-processing preview matched Stripe and the database.
  • Cancellation email step is wired up and gated to just the auto-cancel rows, but doesn't actually send yet since its template doesn't exist (tracked in #1786).

Scope

  • Merge this branch's cron implementation.
  • Put GET /cronjob/process-unsubscribes-table on the production schedule, same way this repo's other cronjobs are scheduled.
  • After #1786 ships, run one more dry_run=1 check and confirm the preview shows the email as sent rather than skipped.

Out of scope

  • PayPal failed-payment detection — separate follow-up issue.
  • The email template itself — #1786.

Risk / test plan

  • Legacy gothru.co cron is already fully shut down, so there's no old process to double-process against — no cutover coordination needed.
  • Let the first automatic run land on a normal day and check its response before trusting it unattended.

issues.display_title: Issue #1790: PayPal Downgrade: transid still stores subscription id (I-...), not capture id
issues.main_description_html:
Update

On the PayPal downgrade subscription flow, transid saved to cc_logs.TransID and cc_purchase.transid still uses the raw PayPal subscription id (I-...) instead of the capture/sale transaction id.

Location

app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/Capture/Actions/DowngradeHandler.php:151-153

$invoiceData = $this->downgradeHelpers->insertCCPurchaseForDowngrade(
    transactionId: $subscription['id'] ?? '',
    customerId: $subscription['subscriber']['payer_id'] ?? null,

$subscription is the raw object from PaypalHelper::getSubscriptionDetails() (line 234), so $subscription['id'] is the subscription id (I-...), not a capture id. This file never calls getSubscriptionTransactions() or any resolver.

This value flows into:

  • DowngradeHelper::insertCCPurchaseForDowngrade → logDowngradeTransaction (DowngradeHelper.php:79 — $this->ccLogClass->TransID = $transactionId;)
  • PaymentHelpers::insertTransaction (PaymentHelpers.php:146 — 'transid' => $params['transaction_id'])

Expected fix

Follow the already-correct pattern in UpgradeHandler.php:502-515 (resolvePaypalUpgradeTransactionId()): fetch the capture/sale transaction id via getSubscriptionTransactions($subscriptionId, $isTestMode), use $transaction['id'], fall back to the subscription id only if the lookup fails.

Reference

Same class of fix already applied to SubscribeHandler.php via PaypalTransIdResolver.php (see docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-paypal-transid-capture-id-design.md, issue #1756) — the Downgrade path was missed by that fix.

Result

Fixed on fix-paypal-downgrade-transid (f099216): added DowngradeHandler::resolvePaypalTransactionId(), mirroring UpgradeHandler's pattern. Tests pass, reviewed, ready to merge.

issues.display_title: Issue #1791: PayPal Buy Storage: transid still stores subscription id (I-...), not capture id
issues.main_description_html:
Update

On the PayPal buy storage add-on flow (which creates a new subscription), transid saved to cc_logs.TransID and cc_purchase.transid still uses the raw PayPal subscription id (I-...) instead of the capture/sale transaction id.

Location

app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/Capture/Actions/BuyStorageHandler.php:190-191

$invoiceData = $this->upgradeHelper->insertCCPurchaseForUpgrade(
    transactionId: $newSubscription['id'],
    customerId: $newSubscription['subscriber']['payer_id'] ?? null,

$newSubscription is the raw subscription detail from PaypalHelper::getSubscriptionDetails($newSubscriptionId, ...) (line 116), so $newSubscription['id'] is the subscription id (I-...). This file's docblock claims it "follows the Upgrade pattern", but it never calls resolvePaypalUpgradeTransactionId() or getSubscriptionTransactions(). The same raw id is also reused in the email field (BuyStorageHandler.php:213 — 'stripeTransactionId' => $newSubscription['id']).

This value flows into:

  • UpgradeHelper::insertCCPurchaseForUpgrade → logToCCLogs (UpgradeHelper.php:333 — $this->ccLogClass->TransID = $transID;)
  • PaymentHelpers::insertTransaction (PaymentHelpers.php:146 — 'transid' => $params['transaction_id'])

Expected fix

Follow the already-correct pattern in UpgradeHandler.php:502-515 (resolvePaypalUpgradeTransactionId()): fetch the capture/sale transaction id via getSubscriptionTransactions($subscriptionId, $isTestMode), use $transaction['id'], fall back to the subscription id only if the lookup fails.

Reference

Same class of fix already applied to SubscribeHandler.php via PaypalTransIdResolver.php (see docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-paypal-transid-capture-id-design.md, issue #1756) — the Buy Storage path was missed by that fix.

Result

Fixed on fix-paypal-buystorage-transid (8a8ebf4): added BuyStorageHandler::resolvePaypalTransactionId(), mirroring UpgradeHandler's pattern. Tests pass (3/3), ready to merge.

issues.display_title: Issue #1797: Reset recurring_profile / current_recurring_plan on hard cancel in UnsubscribesSweeper
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

UnsubscribesSweeper hard-cancels users but leaves stale recurring_profile/current_recurring_plan in user_extra_data.

Current state

UnsubscribesSweeper::processRow() (app/Http/Controllers/Cronjobs/Helpers/UnsubscribesSweeper.php) updates users/users_cc_renewal_dates/unsubscribes on hard cancel but never touches user_extra_data. Legacy cancel_users_account.php did clear it on hard cancel; that step got dropped when the flow was split into Detect + Sweep phases.

Target state

  • On hard cancel (target === 0) only, reset user_extra_data.recurring_profile, pnref, pnref_date ('0000-00-00 00:00:00'), current_recurring_plan — never on a downgrade.
  • Same DB transaction as the other writes; dry_run preview matches real writes.
  • Auto-cancel email keeps real failed-invoice data (snapshot recurring_profile before the reset).

Risk / test plan

dry_run=1&test_mode=1, confirm user_extra_data write only on non-downgrade rows and email still shows real failed-invoice data.

Result

  • processRow(): on target === 0 inside the existing transaction, reset user_extra_data.recurring_profile / pnref to '', pnref_date to '0000-00-00 00:00:00', current_recurring_plan to null. Never touched on a downgrade to a specific plan.
  • Before that write runs, snapshot the row's current recurring_profile (only when not a dry run and unsubscribe_type === '2') so fetchLastFailedInvoice/the auto-cancel email still resolve the real (pre-reset) profile instead of the blanked value.
  • pnref_date reset value fixed to '0000-00-00 00:00:00' (not '') to match the existing convention in Unsubscribe.php for that datetime column and avoid a strict-mode SQL error rolling back the whole row.
  • dry_run preview updated to include the same user_extra_data write, gated the same way, so preview output matches real writes.
  • Branch: fix/unsubscribes-sweeper-reset-recurring-profile (commits 1f8418d46, 54b182104).
